skill.name: set-up-magento-meta-poas-bidding
skill.description: Guide Magento stores through Meta profit bidding with Product Metrics and the Conversions API. Check tracking and cost readiness, then guide the account owner through creating a profit conversion and choosing a starting target.
skill.summary: Set up Meta bidding on Magento order profit instead of revenue.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are documentation links, Markdown formatting, or ordinary setup checks. Real risks include third-party code installation, credential handling, order access, and insufficient approval before writes or live data sharing. No evidence of credential theft or an attempt to override this audit was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Conflicting instructions for collecting the Meta access token
remediation.suggestion: Require direct token entry in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove instructions to request tokens in chat or pass them through shell commands or general assistant tools.

remediation.issue: External installation and remote tools require explicit trust
remediation.suggestion: Keep installs manual and pin the installer and skill revision. Verify the Composer repository and package provenance, and require approval before connecting an authenticated MCP server.

remediation.issue: Write guidance does not consistently require approval
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only checks. Preview the specific company, property, destination, and proposed change, then require confirmation before each state change.

remediation.issue: Order diagnostics can expose more data than needed
remediation.suggestion: Use one user-designated test order. Return only delivery status and whether a profit value is present, without exposing full records or customer details.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs and fallback references are not verified
remediation.suggestion: Validate handoff URLs against approved HTTPS destinations. Bundle or pin the reference text, and treat fetched pages as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Live Meta forwarding is enabled by default during setup
remediation.suggestion: Use a separate test pixel or dataset for verification. Require explicit approval for live forwarding after showing the destination, data fields, and applicable consent requirements.

remediation.issue: Reported profit value can overstate realized contribution
remediation.suggestion: Explain that the break-even target is illustrative. Reconcile ad spend against store contribution that includes signed losses and later refunds before making budget decisions.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Meta Token Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The guide says to enter the access token in the app but also requires the assistant to ask for it. The skill allows forwarding it to a command, which may expose it in transcripts, tool logs, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both references explicitly permit assistant handling of the token. The reviewed instructions do not specify a protected input or transport for that route.

semantic_findings.title: Live Meta Forwarding Lacks a Separate Approval Step
semantic_findings.description: Setup leaves sending enabled when the destination is added, then clears the test code after verification. The guide does not require a distinct approval before live forwarding of consented customer matching data and order values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide states which data is sent and makes the test code optional. It documents shopper consent, but not a separate operator decision to begin live forwarding.

semantic_findings.title: Unversioned Remote Instructions Can Change the Audited Workflow
semantic_findings.description: If bundled references are absent, the assistant is told to fetch live vendor Markdown as a substitute for the setup steps. Changes to those pages can introduce new instructions after the skill revision was reviewed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback is explicit and uses unversioned URLs with no integrity check. No injected remote content was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Reported Profit Can Misstate Campaign Break-Even
semantic_findings.description: The guide labels a 100% goal as break-even, but the event value floors losses at zero and later refunds do not revise Meta events. Relying on that value alone can distort budget decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly describes the break-even target, clamped event value, and refund limitation. The signed profit is a separate parameter, not the configured conversion value.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Profit Bidding for Magento
content.value_statement: A Magento campaign can hit its revenue target and still lose money after product costs and fees. This skill guides you through sending contribution profit to Meta and selecting it as a bidding signal.
actual_capabilities: Read setup progress through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP and identify incomplete connection steps.
Guide a developer through connecting the Magento store view, importing its private configuration, and verifying the module.
Explain how order item costs, shipping, handling, returns, and payment fees affect the reported contribution profit.
Guide the account owner through verifying a test event and creating a Meta custom conversion for PMOrderProfit.
Explain how to estimate a starting profit target from current POAS and how revenue bidding differs.
Troubleshoot missing profit events, incomplete costs, and events that appear only in Meta Test Events.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, appropriate workspace and Meta access, and a Magento module installed by a developer.
The account owner creates and selects the Meta conversion. The assistant does not switch the campaign optimization event.
Unknown costs can prevent a profit event. Meta receives zero conversion value for losses and does not update events for later refunds.
This workflow covers profit and revenue bidding, not new customer, returning customer, or lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Check readiness for profit bidding
use_cases.description: Identify missing store connections, consent settings, or cost inputs before using profit as a bidding signal.

use_cases.title: Review tracking before launch
use_cases.description: Verify module activation, store-view mapping, cron, and delivery of one designated test order.

use_cases.title: Plan a one-campaign pilot
use_cases.description: Compare revenue and profit signals, choose an initial target, and prepare the manual Meta conversion change.

prompt_templates.title: Understand profit bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between revenue and profit bidding for my Magento store. List the accounts, permissions, and cost data I need.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are deciding whether profit bidding fits your store.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Product Metrics setup for my selected Magento store view using read-only operations. List completed steps and what I need to finish manually.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have started connecting your store and Meta pixel.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a missing profit event
prompt_templates.prompt: Check why my designated test order showed revenue but no profit event. Use read-only checks, and report delivery and cost status without showing customer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have an eligible test order, but PMOrderProfit is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled campaign pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a one-campaign profit bidding pilot with current POAS of 1.5. Explain the starting target, manual Meta changes, and how to compare reported values with actual profit. Do not change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have verified profit events and want to test a bidding change.

output_examples.input: My test order reached Meta with revenue but no profit. What should I check?
output: Revenue arrived, but the order does not have a complete contribution margin.
Check item costs and additional costs in Product Metrics. Verify that order currency matches the Magento base currency.
After confirming consent settings and costs, place another test order and check whether the profit event arrives.

output_examples.input: My current profit on ad spend is 1.5. How should I plan the pilot?
output: Consider 150% as a starting target for one campaign. Meta expresses the value target as a ROAS percentage.
After verifying the profit event, the account owner selects its custom conversion and sets the goal.
Compare the reported conversion value with store contribution after costs, losses, and refunds before expanding the pilot.

best_practices: Use the verified Product Metrics app for credential entry and keep Magento configuration files out of chat.
Verify consent, complete costs, and delivery of a designated test order before selecting the profit conversion.
Pilot one campaign and reconcile its reported conversion value with store contribution and ad spend.
anti_patterns: Sharing a Meta access token or Magento private configuration file with the assistant.
Reusing a revenue-based ROAS goal unchanged when switching to a profit conversion.
Treating events in Meta Test Events as proof that live reporting is active.

faq.question: Do I need a developer?
faq.answer: Yes. A developer installs the Product Metrics module on the Magento server and verifies that cron runs.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta can deduplicate browser and server events when their event names and IDs match within 48 hours.

faq.question: Where do I enter my Meta access token?
faq.answer: Enter it directly in the verified Product Metrics app when connecting your Meta destination. Keep it out of chat.

faq.question: Why is PMOrderProfit missing?
faq.answer: Meta must first receive an eligible profit event. Check consent and cost completeness, then verify delivery with a test order.

faq.question: Can I keep bidding on revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the standard Purchase event and a revenue-based ROAS goal instead of the profit conversion.

faq.question: Does Meta revise events after a refund?
faq.answer: No. Later refunds do not revise previously sent Meta events, so reconcile campaign results against store records.
